buildSourceNote: Build 146 carries v1.1.0-rc.23. THE OWNER REPORTED Too many login attempts from this IP via a phone screenshot, and asked who decided that one person mistyping a password can lock out the entire workshop. ANSWER: NOBODY DECIDED IT - it is a defect, not a policy. The login limiter used express-rate-limit's DEFAULT key, which is req.ip. trust proxy is never set in server.ts (there is no app.set trust proxy anywhere) and the TRUST_PROXY env var the deployment docs claim is "Value: 1" is not on the service at all, so Express ignores X-Forwarded-For and req.ip returns the Cloud Run front-end address, identical for every caller. That silently turned 10 attempts per IP into ONE SHARED BUDGET of 10 attempts per 15 minutes for the whole company, staff on mobile data included. The library has been reporting the misconfiguration on every request since the limiter landed: ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR and ERR_ERL_FORWARDED_HEADER, found in Cloud Logging at 2026-09-16T13:48:18Z. OBSERVED: nine failed attempts from two different phones (users 91 and 68) between 12:43 and 12:46 consumed the shared budget and locked everyone else out; login_history shows those two devices were on different IPv6 addresses, so the bucket is not even per-workshop, it is per front-end. ORIGIN: commit b331acd, 2026-07-09, a UI-fixes bundle whose message is about attendance/overtime tabs and font colours - so the limiter was scaffolded rather than reasoned, with no ADR and no decision-log entry, and docs/ mentions rate limiting exactly once in an unrelated line. THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNEW: src/middleware/rate-limiter.ts documents this precise hazard and deliberately avoids it for the AI routes, warning that staff sharing the dealership NAT egress IP would have collapsed the whole workshop into one bucket and throttled each other - the login limiter was left on the library default. THE FIX: keyGenerator now keys on the normalised username, so one person's typos cannot shut anybody else out while brute force against a single account is still throttled, and it no longer depends on the proxy chain; the fallback for a body with no username uses the socket peer rather than req.ip so the library validation cannot fire and such a request cannot lock a real user out; skipSuccessfulRequests means a correct credential no longer counts against the budget; and the message no longer claims to be IP-based. trust proxy is deliberately NOT set here - choosing a value needs the real X-Forwarded-For hop count measured against production first, and a wrong number either preserves this bug or lets a caller spoof its own address. GATES: lint:fabrication PASS (889 files, 0 errors); tsc --noEmit reports the same 9 pre-existing errors, none in server.ts. FOLLOW-UP FLAGGED, NOT DONE: the ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md entry for TRUST_PROXY is wrong and should be corrected or the variable actually wired; and the AI limiter in src/middleware/rate-limiter.ts shares the same in-memory per-instance caveat it documents itself.

THE RATE-LIMITER FIX IS VERIFIED AT RUNTIME, not just by revision: before the fix express-rate-limit emitted ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR and ERR_ERL_FORWARDED_HEADER on EVERY login request (last batch 2026-09-16T13:48:18Z), because the default keyGenerator read req.ip while trust proxy was false. After the deploy, at 2026-09-16T14:33Z, ONE deliberate failed sign-in was sent for the non-existent username zz-rc23-probe-no-such-user; it returned 401 Invalid username or password (so the custom keyGenerator does not break the route), and a search for textPayload:ERR_ERL over the following 15 minutes returned NOTHING - the validation warnings have stopped, which is direct evidence that the key is no longer req.ip. The probe used a non-existent username deliberately: it resolves to no user_id so no login_history row was written and no real account bucket was touched. STILL UNVERIFIED: the actual user-facing behaviour, that two different people mistyping passwords no longer lock each other out - that needs two real sign-ins, and nothing has been signed in since 13:48:18Z. Also outstanding from rc.22: the Approve -> evidence panel on the Attendance screen has not been confirmed in the browser. ALSO FLAGGED, NOT FIXED: deployment/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md documents TRUST_PROXY as Value 1 but the variable is not on the service and no code reads it - the doc is wrong.
